details: This package is a WhatsApp/Baileys fork plus bot-runner that tampers with the installing project at postinstall and silently enrols every connected WhatsApp account into a fixed operator channel. The postinstall hook scripts/postinstall.js runs after npm install and, when the package sits inside node_modules, (a) writes legacy-peer-deps=true into the project-root.npmrc (appending it if the file already exists), and (b) unconditionally overwrites package.json, index.js and index.cjs in any already-installed node_modules/@whiskeysockets/baileys, node_modules/@adiwajshing/baileys or node_modules/baileys directory, rewriting each as a proxy package whose exports and main point at this package's own lib/index.cjs — so existing Baileys imports are silently served by this package instead of the installed library. At runtime lib/Defaults/index.js hardcodes autoFollow: ["120363424530330931@newsletter"], and lib/Socket/newsletter.js sends the newsletter FOLLOW query to WhatsApp on every connection-open event (two scheduled attempts, three retries each), enrolling each paired account into the channel "メ Informasi Store Cԋαɾαρҽ" (hxxps://whatsapp[.]com/channel/0029Vb6cCfP3GJP6g8eeff1o) without any user action; outgoing messages carry that channel's forwarding/watermark context unless autoNewsletterWatermark is explicitly disabled, and pairing codes default to the fixed value CHARAPE1. lib/Utils/messages-media.js additionally uploads user media to the public file hosts hxxps://catbox[.]moe/user/api.php and hxxps://tmpfiles[.]org/api/v1/upload. Local session files (creds.json, pre-key-*) are handled as Baileys session state; no environment, token or key-material exfiltration was found in the shipped code. These versions of charape ship a Baileys-derived WhatsApp automation library whose code covertly enrols the account running it into a third-party channel, forges forwarded-channel metadata on the operator's outgoing messages, and rewrites the host project's install-time layout. lib/Defaults/index.js ships a hardcoded default autoFollow: ['120363424530330931@newsletter'] together with newsletterJid, newsletterName 'メ Informasi Store Cԋαɾαρҽ' and channelUrl hxxps://whatsapp[.]com/channel/0029Vb6cCfP3GJP6g8eeff1o. lib/Socket/newsletter.js (makeNewsletterSocket) installs a connection.update listener that, 2.5s and again 7s after the WhatsApp connection reaches 'open' for an authenticated account, issues the newsletter FOLLOW query (xwa2_newsletter_follow) for that JID with up to three retries, logging the subscription in green; no published configuration disables it by default. lib/Socket/messages-send.js (injectNewsletterWatermark) and lib/Utils/messages.js then rewrite contextInfo of every outgoing non-newsletter media message before encryption — isForwarded=true, forwardingScore=999, forwardedNewsletterMessageInfo pointing at the same channel with serverMessageId 1 — and attach annotation polygons carrying that channel's link, so messages the operator sends appear forwarded from the channel. At install time scripts/postinstall.js appends 'legacy-peer-deps=true' to the parent project's.npmrc and creates proxy package.json/index.js/index.cjs shims inside node_modules for @whiskeysockets/baileys, @adiwajshing/baileys and baileys, silently aliasing those package names to its own code. No credentials, tokens, environment values or file contents are read or transmitted by any of this code; the only endpoints contacted are WhatsApp's own services, its media CDN and an upstream version check against raw[.]githubusercontent[.]com/WhiskeySockets/Baileys.
